items.title: XRISM Sees a Star’s Wind Power Its Companion’s Flares
items.body: NASA reports that astronomers using the Japan-led XRISM observatory directly observed a giant star’s stellar wind being captured by its compact companion, powering strong X-ray flares. The target is BP Crucis, a high-mass X-ray binary about 13,000 light-years away in the southern constellation Crux.

items.body: Ars, citing Reuters, reports that US officials removed a Chinese AI search tool briefly deployed on the Federal Register after social-media users noticed the National Archives was using Alibaba’s Qwen. The point is not that one number is fake; each answers a different accounting question.

items.title: Two Profit Measures, Two Different Stories
items.body: Econbrowser reports that corporate net income after tax surged, particularly in the second quarter. Its adjusted, pre-tax profit measure had not clearly changed nearly as much. That contrast is a warning against treating every line called “profit” as a clean read on underlying sector momentum.

discussion.body: The key marker is “good for”: well-being concerns a person’s own life, rather than goodness in general.
So “Is this morally admirable?” and “Is this good for the person?” are different questions, not synonyms.

items.title: Well-Being Is About What Makes a Life Go Well
items.body: Philosophical well-being asks how well a person’s life is going for that person: which ultimate goods make it worth living from their point of view. It is prudential value, distinct from moral or aesthetic value.

sources.title: Many Jewish faculty and staff say university EDI is failing them

discussion.body: An office can exist on paper yet leave people feeling unprotected. The respondents' accounts make that gap the issue.
The surveys address different groups and questions. An overall measure of students' attitudes cannot resolve whether particular complaints were handled adequately.

items.title: Canadian Jewish faculty say university EDI offices met them with silence after Oct. 7
items.body: The Conversation reports that a study of Jewish faculty and staff at Canadian universities found many respondents felt EDI offices met their concerns with silence or dismissal after October 7, 2023. A separate federally commissioned survey of Jewish students found dissatisfaction with those offices. A third survey found that Canadian university students generally expressed low negativity toward Jews and high negativity toward Israel. In 2025, Jewish people were the target of 70 per cent of police-reported hate crimes directed at a religious group in Canada, despite making up about one per cent of the population.

items.title: NASA's COSI telescope will hunt gamma rays from antimatter and dying stars
items.body: The Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI) is coming together at UC Berkeley. This wide-field gamma-ray telescope will study the Milky Way's most energetic phenomena: the creation and destruction of matter and antimatter, and the final stages of stellar lives. The detector assembly — seen in a July 8 image being lifted into place — uses flex circuits covered in silver material to carry signals to readout electronics. It's a collaboration spanning UC Berkeley's Space Sciences Lab, UC San Diego, the Naval Research Laboratory, NASA Goddard, Northrop Grumman, Space Dynamics Laboratory, the Italian Space Agency, and other institutions.

Advising controllers and replacing their decisions are different roles. That distinction matters when judging what this rollout is meant to accomplish.

items.title: FAA to debut AI air-traffic advisor over Washington, D.C. as soon as Monday
items.body: The FAA's SMART system — an AI tool that predicts traffic flows and flags potential conflicts using airline schedules, weather, airport capacity, and airspace conditions — could go live for the three major D.C.-area airports on September 21. It's the first step toward a planned nationwide rollout across the 29 million square miles of U.S. airspace. Aviation safety consultant Philip Mann, a 17-year FAA veteran, called the limited-scope launch the 'right call' before scaling nationally.

sources.title: What Came Before the American Suburb?

discussion.body: The railroad was more than a way out of town: arriving passengers also helped sustain the shops in town.
That makes the later shift toward malls a change in where people gathered and spent money, as well as a change in how they travelled.

items.title: What the American landscape looked like before the suburb took over
items.body: Hempstead Village offers a view of small-town America before postwar suburban expansion. Under Dutch colonial control, John Carman and John Fordham negotiated a land purchase with local Indigenous tribes in 1643; families arrived the following year. Centuries later, railroad connections helped sustain the village's commercial life by bringing people into its downtown shopping district. After World War II, nearby Levittown and shopping malls such as Roosevelt Field helped shift the area's development and drew shoppers away from historic commercial centers.

That does not make the profit increase imaginary. It means the measure needs to match the question being asked.

items.title: After‑tax manufacturing profits surge, but adjusted measures tell a mixed story
items.body: EJ Antoni highlighted a surge in corporate net income after tax. Econbrowser's author contrasts that figure with manufacturing profits adjusted for inventory valuation and argues that tax treatment can raise after-tax income without demonstrating higher underlying productivity. The disagreement turns on what the chosen profit measure actually tells us about manufacturing performance.
